headline.title: Pre-season: still too mild.
headline.text: None of the resorts close to opening get cold enough to make snow this week. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Warm temperatures continue through Wednesday with potential for exceeding a few daily records Wednesday afternoon. Shower chances remain Tuesday afternoon.
Rain is expected from Thursday into Friday morning. Somewhat more uncertain is additional rain Friday afternoon through Saturday night.

ALY.excerpt: ) Temperatures trend above normal this week with mostly dry weather through Wednesday before chances for rain increase Thursday into Thursday night as a cold front arrives. Depending on if and when the front slows down, there is a low to medium chance in rain showers continuing into Friday and the weekend.

GYX.excerpt:
Outside of some light showers in the mountains, conditions will stay mostly dry through mid week with above normal temperatures.
The first chance in several weeks of a soaking rainfall arrives late this week.

BUF.excerpt:
) Warm and dry today. Showers possible tonight and Tuesday.
) Unseasonably mild Wednesday, unsettled weather returns Thursday.

PHI.excerpt:
Some areas of frost again overnight. Aside from potential for nocturnal fog development tonight and Tuesday night, generally tranquil weather is expected to prevail through the middle of the week.
Rain chances return late this week and into the weekend.

CTP.excerpt: ) Unseasonably mild and dry weather will continue until late Wednesday or Wednesday Night prior to a few periods of showers preceding and accompanying a cold frontal passage. Cooler and a return to mainly dry conditions will follow for Friday through Sunday.

RLX.excerpt: ) Some showers today, but more widespread and significant precipitation Wednesday into Thursday.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Quiet and mild.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:31}} to {{t:58}}, with rain at times.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Nights stay too mild to make much snow this week.

NWS Burlington forecasters, Monday 2:24 AM: "Warm temperatures continue through Wednesday with potential for exceeding a few daily records Wednesday afternoon. Shower chances remain Tuesday afternoon."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and near-normal precipitation.
